figures.caption: Fig. 2: The proposed ReasonSeg-SGDR benchmark. It focuses on the joint use of visual perception and high-level reasoning. It spans multiple dimensions, including discriminative, geometric, spatial, and multi-step reasoning, all of which require finegrained mask generation. The target region is identified by carefully examining the image and reasoning over the visual evidence.

Fig. 1: Comparison of different MLLM-based segmentation methods. Prior methods either (a) use language outputs as spatial prompts for mask generation, or (b) connect latent embeddings from MLLMs to a mask decoder in an end-to-end manner. (c) We propose a two-stage framework for mask generation and selection, reformulating image segmentation as candidate discovery followed by discriminative mask selection.

Table 4: Ablation studies on mask evaluator. We investigate the impact of several factors, including MLLM scale, the contribution of the proposed dataset, and increased test-time computation with CoT.
Table 3: Ablation studies on candidate mask generator. We ablate over the proposed strategies for candidate discovery.

Fig. 3: The overall framework of Rea2Seg. Rea2Seg consists of an attention-driven candidate mask generator and a mask evaluator for selection. Specifically, (1) candidate regions are first identified based on the attention maps of a segmentation MLLM; (2) an MLLM then performs reasoning and assigns scores to all candidate masks; and (3) the candidates are reranked, and the highest-scoring mask is selected as the final output. Rea2Seg reformulates mask generation as a reasoning-based and discriminative mask understanding problem.
